tldr: Headlines split between two dominant registers: health-and-proof-of-life (UK, Germany, Brazil, Canada) and political-coup context (AFP, France 24 Spanish, NDTV, and most outlets using 'detained' to signal political imprisonment). NPR (USA) is the sole outlet to pivot to a human-emotional frame ('give her family hope'), while CGTN (China) is the sole outlet to strip all political and health framing, using Suu Kyi's official pre-coup title and presenting the ICRC visit as a neutral diplomatic event.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only outlet to foreground the family-hope angle in the headline itself ('give her family hope'), pivoting entirely away from the health-concern or political-coup frames dominant elsewhere — a human-emotional register absent from every other title in the corpus.

The only outlet to use Suu Kyi's official pre-coup title 'former State Counsellor' without any 'detained', 'ousted', or coup framing, presenting the ICRC visit as a neutral bilateral meeting rather than a humanitarian access event or proof-of-life moment — and the reason the china bucket goes to silences.

The only outlet to frame the visit as a response to external pressure ('Myanmar military pushed to prove she is alive'), implying international accountability and coercion of the junta rather than a health-confirmation or humanitarian-access story — the starkest adversarial headline in the corpus.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, coverage splits between a health-and-isolation register (UK, Germany, Brazil, Canada) and a political-coup register (AFP, France 24 Spanish, NDTV); China's diplomatic neutrality and NPR's family-hope pivot are the sharpest headline-layer departures from this two-pole consensus.
